AheadAlert.description:
One thing ahead of the airplane (vfr.alerts): airspace, a special-
use area or a TFR its track goes into in the next five minutes, or the
ground or an obstacle it comes within 500 ft of in the next minute.
`seconds` and `distance_nm` are how long and how far until it at the
ground speed, 0 where it is now; `lat`/`lon` where the track meets it
(the obstacle itself, the ground's highest point).
AheadAlert.title: AheadAlert

AircraftBases.description:
Where airplanes are based (vfr.traffic.based): the field their last
flights keep to, or None where none; those still being looked up are
pending, given on a later ask.
AircraftBases.title: AircraftBases

AircraftProfile.description:
The aircraft's name plus its performance profile -- every field a
data/aircraft/*.json file carries, declared, so a page reads them as
fields rather than guessing at a dict. The three figures after the
name are required when a profile is loaded (REQUIRED_FIELDS in
vfr.aircraft); the rest fall back to defaults in vfr.navlog when a
profile leaves them out. `extra="allow"` keeps a field a newer
profile adds on its way through.
AircraftProfile.title: AircraftProfile

AircraftProfileSummary.description: One of data/aircraft/*.json, for the nav log's aircraft picker.
AircraftProfileSummary.title: AircraftProfileSummary

AircraftRegistration.description:
A US airplane's record in the FAA's aircraft registry (vfr.registry,
the Releasable Aircraft Database): who it is registered to and where,
what it is, its engine, and its registration's and airworthiness
certificates. The owner's town, never the street; an owner who asked
the FAA to withhold their name (49 U.S.C. 44114(b)) is not in it.
AircraftRegistration.title: AircraftRegistration

AirplaneInspections.description:
The pilot's own airplane's inspections and tests as its owner
recorded them on the gateway: each its last good day, "yyyy-mm-dd".
AirplaneInspections.title: AirplaneInspections

AirplaneLoad.description:
What the pilot loads (lib/weightBalance Load): the airplane's own
empty weight and arm, each station's pounds in the loading's order,
and the fuel at the start, gallons.
AirplaneLoad.title: AirplaneLoad

AirportEnd.description:
A point of the route: an airport, or -- a stop only -- a named fix
flown through (`kind` "fix": a VFR or GPS waypoint, its `name` the
kind of fix it is, no elevation).
AirportEnd.title: AirportEnd

AirportPhotos.description:
The pictures an airport's card swipes through behind its diagram:
its aerial from the USGS, every field's, and a photo from the ground
where there is a free one.
AirportPhotos.title: AirportPhotos

AirportPin.description:
A landing field the map can open a card for: the ident pilots use,
where it is, and its size -- the bigger ones are kept when a wide
view holds more than the map asks for. `flight_category` is the
field's METAR's (VFR, MVFR, IFR, LIFR), for the map's weather chip:
None where it has no reporting station, or the weather could not be
asked. `military` is a field the armed services own (the FAA's
airport file, vfr.faa_data.military_fields): "military" where a civil
airplane lands only with the service's permission, "joint" where a
civil airport shares it; None for every other field.
AirportPin.title: AirportPin

AirportPlace.description:
One airport the way the map's card shows it: its name and place,
the class of the airspace over it, whether it has a tower, its
runways and radio, and the weather there now. `metar` is None for a
field with no reporting station, and `weather_unavailable` says the
weather service could not be asked at all -- not the same thing.
AirportPlace.title: AirportPlace

AirportServices.description:
What a field offers a pilot who lands there: from its Chart
Supplement entry (NASR's APT_BASE and its remarks) the fuel, fees,
parking, repair and oxygen, and from Overture Maps (vfr.nearby) the
places to eat, sleep and hire a car within five miles.
`nearby_unavailable` where Overture could not be read: not the same
as nothing near.
AirportServices.title: AirportServices

AirportSuggestion.description:
An airport the search answers -- or, asked with `fixes`, a named
fix (`kind` "fix": a VFR waypoint, a GPS waypoint), its `name` the
kind of fix and its `region` the state it is in.
AirportSuggestion.title: AirportSuggestion

AirspaceAt.description:
The airspace over a point on the chart, from the ground up: the
classes in bands, the Mode C veil, the special-use areas and the
TFRs there. `ground_ft` is the ground's height the AGL floors were
placed from (Terrain Tiles); None where it could not be read, and
the bands are then measured from sea level. Either source of areas
out is said so rather than shown as none.
AirspaceAt.title: AirspaceAt

AirspaceBand.description:
One class of airspace over a point, from `floor_ft` to
`ceiling_ft` MSL (vfr.airspace_at): its name where it is a B, C or
D; the VFR minimums in it (None in A); what it takes to go in; the
equipment it asks for; and the 91.117 speed limit there.
AirspaceBand.title: AirspaceBand

AirspaceTransit.description:
Controlled airspace the route passes through: a radio call to
make, not a ceiling constraint.
AirspaceTransit.title: AirspaceTransit

AirspaceVolume.description:
One Class B, C or D volume in the map's view (vfr.airspace_map):
one shelf of a Class B, the surface area or a shelf of a Class C, or
a Class D, with its altitudes as the FAA's Class Airspace file has
them and its boundary as lines of [lat, lon] clipped to the box.
AirspaceVolume.title: AirspaceVolume

AirwayAltitudes.description:
An airway segment's published altitudes, feet MSL (NASR AWY_SEG_ALT):
the MEA, the GNSS MEA, the MOCA and the MAA; `from_` the fix it starts
at.
AirwayAltitudes.title: AirwayAltitudes

AlertsAhead.title: AlertsAhead

AlternateCheck.description:
A field as the IFR alternate (14 CFR 91.169(c)): its forecast at the
ETA there against its minimums -- 600 and 2 with a precision approach,
800 and 2 without -- `good` True or False, or None where the pilot has
to look (its own published alternate minimums, no approach, no TAF).
AlternateCheck.title: AlternateCheck

AlternateLeg.description:
The leg from the destination on to the IFR alternate: flown at the
route's last altitude in its winds, or in still air where they could
not be read (`still_air`).
AlternateLeg.title: AlternateLeg

Alternates.description:
GET /api/alternate: the destination's check, the pilot's alternate's
and the nearest fields that will do.
Alternates.title: Alternates

AltitudeBreakdown.description:
The full reasoning behind one recommended cruise altitude.
`low_ceiling_or_visibility` is None, not False, when the forecast
call itself failed: unknown must not read as confirmed fine.
`candidates_ft` are every legal altitude for the whole route;
`segments` the same leg by leg, present when the nav log's fixes
were known.
AltitudeBreakdown.title: AltitudeBreakdown

AltitudeCaution.description:
An altitude the pilot set for a hop (`from_ident` to `to_ident`) and
what is wrong with it against the planner's band there
(app.planning.own_altitude_caution): a warning, not a refusal.
AltitudeCaution.title: AltitudeCaution

AltitudeFigure.description:
The route flown at one altitude, for the altitude wheel (the owner's
pick, 2026-10-20): each leg at it where it is legal there, else at the
leg's nearest legal altitude (`everywhere` false then); the times and
fuel with the climbs, the wind along the legs, positive helping.
AltitudeFigure.title: AltitudeFigure

AltitudeOption.description:
One of the four plans -- lowest, highest, fastest, economical --
as its steps and what it costs. `ete_min` is the flying time with every climb
flown (`climb_penalty_min` is how many of those minutes are climb),
the figure the plans are compared on; `tailwind_kt` the
distance-weighted wind component along the course, positive helping,
over the legs that had wind data.
AltitudeOption.title: AltitudeOption

AltitudeSegment.description:
One leg's own band: its floor, the shelf and the clouds over it
alone, and the legal cruising altitudes between -- what lets a plan
step down under a Class B shelf and climb again past it.
AltitudeSegment.title: AltitudeSegment

AltitudeStep.description: Consecutive legs flown at one altitude.
AltitudeStep.title: AltitudeStep

Briefing.description:
`weather_unavailable` names which of hazards/forecast/metars/tfrs
come from a call that failed rather than one that found nothing: an
empty `hazards` must not read the same as "no hazards reported".
Briefing.title: Briefing

Candidate.description:
A scored detection off the chart (app.scoring): `id` its kind and
place, `name` the FAA's for an airport and the kind of thing for
the rest. `selected` is set by the server's greedy pass.
Candidate.title: Candidate

ChartInfo.description:
Which chart the map draws and where its tiles are: the map with no
route on it yet asks for this alone (/api/chart), and a Course
carries it as well.
ChartInfo.title: ChartInfo

ChartLayer.description:
One kind of FAA chart the map can draw and the zooms it has
tiles for: the sectional and the IFR enroute charts as base layers
(`base`), the terminal area chart as an overlay.
ChartLayer.title: ChartLayer

ChartModelSnapshot.description:
The promoted chart model (vfr.chartmodel), against what it has to
beat on the ratings it held out: the palette's constants
(`palette_held_out_mae`) and the training ratings' mean. The
planner's checkpoints move onto the chart once it beats the
palette.
ChartModelSnapshot.title: ChartModelSnapshot

ChartPage.description:
One page of one of the FAA's charts, to show in the app: its
picture is /api/faa-chart/page/{source}/{edition}/{pdf}/{page}.png,
`width` by `height` pixels (vfr.publications.chart_page_png).
ChartPage.title: ChartPage

ChartPages.description:
The pages of an FAA chart the app shows, in order: every page of a
chart of its own, a booklet's pages for the field, a Chart Supplement
entry's pages (vfr.publications.chart_pages).
ChartPages.title: ChartPages

ChartSheet.description:
One sheet of an overlay chart kind and where it is: the map
offers to pin the terminal area chart when the view is over one.
ChartSheet.title: ChartSheet

ChartsStatus.description:
`cycle` is the edition the map draws; `current_cycle` the one
the FAA is on. They differ while a newer cycle is being fetched
and rendered (`building`, `refresh_running`); the map switches
once every tile of the new one is there.
ChartsStatus.title: ChartsStatus

CheckpointPass.description:
A checkpoint: minutes from the takeoff it was due and was passed (or
landed at), None where the plan had no time or the track never got
there; its closest, nm; how late (+) or early, and `ok`, within the
tolerance (None where either time is not known).
CheckpointPass.title: CheckpointPass

Checkpoints.description:
Every hop's candidates and selected checkpoints in order along the
whole route (app.scoring.route_checkpoints), its along-track
distances running on through each stop.
Checkpoints.title: Checkpoints

ClassBAirport.description:
One Class B airport: where it is, and what the weather is doing
there.

Every weather field is optional and often absent. A field with no
current report has no flight category; a field with no TAF issued
has no forecast. Absent is the honest answer -- a pilot must not
read "no data" as "nothing to worry about", so the UI shows the gap
rather than a default.
ClassBAirport.title: ClassBAirport

ClassBResponse.description:
Every Class B airport in one answer -- see the router for why it
is one call rather than one per marker.
ClassBResponse.title: ClassBResponse

Classification.description: What the chart draws at one point; None where it has no coverage.
Classification.title: Classification

Course.description:
The course: the departure, the stops it lands at on the way (in
order; none for a route flown straight), the destination, the whole
distance stop by stop, the bearing out of the departure, and the line
through every stop.
Course.title: Course

Debrief.description:
The flight debriefed: its takeoff and landing (ms since 1970), its
time in the air and the plan's, leg by leg, the checkpoints and the
patterns, the profile flown and planned, the line for the map, and
notes on what does not fit.
Debrief.title: Debrief

DebriefAnswer.description: The debrief, or None where the track never flew faster than taxiing.
DebriefAnswer.title: DebriefAnswer

DebriefAsk.description:
The saved flight's checkpoints and its track's points in time order,
as many as the gateway keeps (TrackDto: 2 to 5,000).
DebriefAsk.title: DebriefAsk

DebriefCheckpoint.description:
A saved flight's checkpoint, as the gateway keeps it
(FlightCheckpointDto): its place and the plan's figures into it.
DebriefCheckpoint.title: DebriefCheckpoint

DebriefPoint.description:
A point of the flown track (TrackDto): when, ms since 1970; GPS
altitude, feet above sea level, where the file has one.
DebriefPoint.title: DebriefPoint

DebriefTolerances.description:
ACS PA.VI.A's and PA.III.B's tolerances the debrief holds the flight
to, for the page's headings.
DebriefTolerances.title: DebriefTolerances

DemonstratedCrosswind.description:
The strongest crosswind the POH says the aeroplane was shown to
take off and land in: not a limitation, but past it the pilot is
beyond what was tested.
DemonstratedCrosswind.title: DemonstratedCrosswind

DestinationCheck.description:
The destination against 14 CFR 91.169(b)'s "1-2-3": an instrument
approach published, and its TAF an hour either side of the ETA a
ceiling of 2,000 ft or more and 3 sm or more -- else an alternate is
`required`, `reasons` saying why (vfr.alternates).
DestinationCheck.title: DestinationCheck

DetectError.description:
The corridor read failed after the stream had started; always the
last line.
DetectError.title: DetectError

Detection.description:
A point the chart-vision detector found. `rating`/`role` are None
until a pick claims it; `rated` is derived from the rating, as a
Pick's is, rather than set beside it. `score` is the palette's
constant for its kind; `predicted_score` the chart model's rating
for it (vfr.chartmodel), None while none is promoted or the corridor
is still being read for the first time.
Detection.title: Detection

Detour.description:
A named fix that keeps a route out of the Class B airspace it is
stopped by (vfr.airspace.detour_waypoint), and where it goes in the
stops: before the stop at `stop_index`, so on the hop it is for.
Detour.title: Detour

DevService.description:
One service the developer console links to, and whether it is up.

`state` is Docker's own word for it -- running, exited, created --
or "absent" where compose has never created the container at all,
which needs `docker compose up -d <service>` once rather than a
start.
DevService.title: DevService

DevServiceStarted.description:
`started` is false when there was nothing to do, which is the
common case: the console asks on every click so the link always
works.
DevServiceStarted.title: DevServiceStarted

DevServices.description:
`available` is false where there is no Docker socket, which is
every deployment that is not the local development stack. The
console stops offering to start anything rather than offering a
button that cannot work.
DevServices.title: DevServices

DisplacedPick.description:
A pick on another point that a save took the place of: the store
keeps one pick per place (vfr.routecsv.SAME_PLACE_NM), whatever each
point is.
DisplacedPick.title: DisplacedPick

DistanceTable.description:
One weight's distances, by pressure altitude (rows) and
temperature (columns).
DistanceTable.title: DistanceTable

Diversion.description:
To a field from a point, in the planner's air there: the field, the
air it is flown in (`wind` None where no forecast was near: worked
with none), the solution and its steps in words, or `problem` where no
heading holds; and each estimate given, checked.
Diversion.title: Diversion

DiversionSolved.description:
The diversion worked out: true course and distance, the correction
(+ right), true and magnetic heading, ground speed, minutes and gallons.
DiversionSolved.title: DiversionSolved

EstimateCheck.description:
A student's estimate against the exact figure: reasonable within its
allowance, and the figure written as the drill writes it.
EstimateCheck.title: EstimateCheck

FieldBelowVfr.description:
A field whose weather is below VFR where the flight meets it
(app.exposure.fields_below_vfr): an airport flown from or to whose
METAR reports IFR or LIFR now, or a TAF station along the route
forecast under 14 CFR 91.155's basic minimums for when the airplane
is there, with the ceiling and visibility that put it there.
FieldBelowVfr.title: FieldBelowVfr

FixPin.description: A fix on the low-altitude enroute chart (NASR's FIX_BASE).
FixPin.title: FixPin

FlightArrival.description: The field an airplane has landed at, and when it was last heard (Unix seconds).
FlightArrival.title: FlightArrival

FlightDeparted.description: The field a flight took off from, and when (Unix seconds).
FlightDeparted.title: FlightDeparted

FlightDetail.description:
An airplane and its flight today (vfr.traffic.flight): what it is,
who flies it, where it took off from where its track shows that, and
its track since, from adsb.lol's open data (ODbL 1.0); and a US
airplane's FAA registration.
FlightDetail.title: FlightDetail

FlightRoute.description:
The route a flight number is scheduled to fly (vfr.traffic.route),
from Virtual Radar Server's route database (CC0): the airports in
order, and whether the airplane is on or near it now. Not the flight
plan filed for today's flight.
FlightRoute.title: FlightRoute

FlightStatus.description:
An airplane's state now, for the alerts a pilot sets on it
(vfr.traffic.status): how long since it was heard, whether it is in
the air -- and where, as the map draws it -- the field it took off
from, and, not in the air, the field it has landed at; from adsb.lol's
open data (ODbL 1.0).
FlightStatus.title: FlightStatus

FoodDetails.description:
A restaurant's stars, reviews and photos from Google Places, for the
map's fly-in food (app.routers.food_details).
FoodDetails.title: FoodDetails

FoodPhoto.description: A restaurant's photo on Google's servers, and whom to credit.
FoodPhoto.title: FoodPhoto

ForecastStation.description:
A TAF station near the route: the worst it forecasts over the
whole flight (`ceiling_ft`, `visibility_sm`, the go/no-go read), and
-- placed along the route -- when the flight gets there and the worst
it forecasts within an hour of then, with the TAF as issued.
ForecastStation.title: ForecastStation

ForecastWind.description:
The wind a TAF forecasts at a field for a time (vfr.weather.
forecast_wind): its own TAF's, else the nearest station's within 30
nm (`ident`, `distance_nm`). From true north; `dir_true_deg` None for
a variable wind. `valid_from` and `valid_to`, the period's, s since
1970.
ForecastWind.title: ForecastWind

FuelStop.description:
A field with the airplane's fuel a flight can land at for it, with
its reserve left (vfr.fuelstops).
FuelStop.title: FuelStop

FuelStopSuggestion.description:
The stops that take one flight short of fuel to its destination with
the reserve left at every landing, the tanks filled at each, and other
fields the first could be. `reason` is "fuel": breaks for a meal or a
rest are the pilot's to pick from the map's Stops.
FuelStopSuggestion.title: FuelStopSuggestion

GAirmet.description:
A G-AIRMET the route crosses during the flight
(app.exposure.gairmets): the hazard in words, its severity
and cause, the time its snapshot is valid at, and its altitudes --
`from_freezing_level` where it starts there.
GAirmet.title: GAirmet

GoNoGo.description:
POST /api/go-no-go: the line over the findings and each finding,
with what the Brief's Risk and Loading pages show beside them.
GoNoGo.title: GoNoGo

GoNoGoAsk.description:
The route, as /api/navlog is asked it (PlanQuery's fields), and what
only the pilot knows.
GoNoGoAsk.title: GoNoGoAsk

GoogleMaps.description: The browser key for Google's Map Tiles API (routers/basemaps).
GoogleMaps.title: GoogleMaps

GroundPhoto.description:
A field's photo from the ground, from its Wikipedia article's lead
image on Wikimedia Commons (vfr.airport_photos), with its credit.
GroundPhoto.title: GroundPhoto

Hazard.description:
A SIGMET/AIRMET whose polygon the route line crosses; in the
briefing, with where and when the flight meets it.
Hazard.title: Hazard

Holding.description:
A hold's entry by AIM 5-3-8 and its steps in words, the other entry
within 5 degrees of a sector's edge, where the airplane comes from
round the fix (for drawing), and the legs in the wind where one was
given -- or `wind_problem` where it is stronger than the airplane.
Holding.title: Holding

HoldingWind.description:
The legs in the wind: the inbound leg's minutes, each leg's heading,
correction and ground speed, the outbound time by the speeds and by the
rule of a second a knot, seconds, and each row's line in words.
HoldingWind.title: HoldingWind

HopTotals.description: One flight between two landings of a route with stops.
HopTotals.title: HopTotals

InboundRadio.description:
The frequency a pilot calls a field on, inbound: `kind` "TWR",
"CTAF" or "UNICOM", and the frequency in MHz.
InboundRadio.title: InboundRadio

Leg.description:
One dead-reckoning leg. `wind` is None when no winds-aloft station
is near enough, which is not the same as calm: groundspeed then falls
back to true airspeed. groundspeed/ETE/fuel are None when the wind
exceeds true airspeed, i.e. the leg cannot be flown.

The true airspeed and fuel flow are the aeroplane's in the leg's own
air (vfr.performance): its cruise figures are at a reference
altitude on a standard day, and the forecast temperature at this
altitude gives the density altitude they are flown at, at the power
it allows -- the cruise power, or less where full throttle cannot
make it. `oat_c` is None where no forecast temperature was near: a
standard day is assumed there.
Leg.title: Leg

LegGrade.description:
A leg graded: the share of its cruise within the altitude tolerance
and of its way within the course tolerance (0 to 1, None where none was
graded), its furthest off each (altitude + high, distance + right), and
`ok`, neither past its tolerance.
LegGrade.title: LegGrade

LegHold.description:
A hold the pilot put at a point of the route (vfr.holds), on the
leg that leaves it -- `at_end`, the leg into the destination it is
held at: its inbound course (magnetic), its turns, its legs by time or
distance, how long (turns, or minutes), the minutes and fuel it takes,
already in the leg's `ete_min` and `fuel_gal` (plan.with_holds), one
turn round its racetrack's minutes, the entry from the course flown to
it (AIM 5-3-8), and that one turn as [lat, lon] pairs from the point.
LegHold.title: LegHold

LegProcedure.description:
A leg flown by the procedures picked -- out by a departure, in by an
arrival and an approach (vfr.procedure_paths.flown) -- rather than as
the route goes: its path from the leg's start, [lat, lon] pairs; the
altitude the chart sets at each point (None where it sets none); its
length; whether it comes down to a runway; where its final starts, the
index in `path` of its final approach fix; where its missed approach
point is, the index in `path` the missed approach is flown from (short
of the runway's threshold, where the path ends, on a VOR's or a LOC's
approach); and the approach's missed approach. The miles it is more than the leg's own, and the time and
fuel they take at the leg's ground speed and cruise burn, are in the
leg's `ete_min` and `fuel_gal` (plan.with_procedures).
LegProcedure.title: LegProcedure

LinePoint.description:
The flight as flown, for the map: `off` where it was outside a
tolerance there.
LinePoint.title: LinePoint

LoadBalance.description:
The weight and balance for the load used: the pilot's, or the
POH's sample airplane where none was sent.
LoadBalance.title: LoadBalance

Loading.description:
How the aeroplane is loaded (its POH's weight and balance): the
weight limits, a sample empty weight and moment (each aeroplane's own
is on its weight and balance record), the stations and their arms,
the fuel's, and the centre-of-gravity envelope as (arm, weight)
corners.
Loading.title: Loading

LostComms.description:
91.185: VFR's words, the routes in the rule's order, each segment's
altitude and why, and when to leave the clearance limit.
LostComms.title: LostComms

LostCommsAsk.description:
The clearance and the route's segments: the altitude assigned, the
one to expect and from which segment on, each segment's minimum for
IFR operations, and for leaving the limit whether it is a fix an
approach begins from, the EFC and the ETA as the pilot writes them.
LostCommsAsk.title: LostCommsAsk

MapLayerAges.description:
When the planner fetched what the map's weather layers are drawn
from (ISO 8601 UTC; None before the first fetch): the METARs the
airports' flight categories come from, and the TFRs.
MapLayerAges.title: MapLayerAges

MissedApproachPath.description:
An approach's missed approach as it is flown, from its missed
approach point and round its hold once (vfr.procedure_paths.missed_path),
and the altitude it climbs to: the highest its fixes set.
MissedApproachPath.title: MissedApproachPath

ModeCVeil.description: The Class B primary airport whose 30 nm Mode C veil the point is in.
ModeCVeil.title: ModeCVeil

ModelComparisonEntry.description:
`metric` names which number `score` is: cv_mae for the sklearn
family and Spark, held_out_mae for PyTorch/TensorFlow. Lower is
better either way.
ModelComparisonEntry.title: ModelComparisonEntry

ModelledWeather.description:
The weather at a field as the NWS's Gridded LAMP models it for the
hour (vfr.glmp), for one with no report of its own: the ceiling above
the ground (None with none), the visibility (10 sm and more is "10"),
their flight category (AIM 7-1-7), and the hour it is for. Planning
guidance, not an observation.
ModelledWeather.title: ModelledWeather

NavLogAltitude.description:
Which altitudes the legs that follow fly. `flown` is the planner's
plan of that name, or "custom" for a pilot's own altitude; None when
the winds the legs need could not be read, so no leg follows -- the
stream's next line is the error. `altitude_ft` is the first leg's (a
plan may step), and None exactly when `flown` is. `options` are the
four plans, offered beside a pilot's own as well; empty only when the
winds failed before they could be made.

It used to say all of that with `choice: null` and an empty `options`,
which a winds outage produced too: the page showed "0 ft · yours",
with Custom pressed, for an altitude nobody typed.
NavLogAltitude.title: NavLogAltitude

NavLogError.description:
The stream's failure. `retry` False where asking again gets the
same answer -- a route with no legal altitude -- so the page offers
no Try again for it. For that one `detail` is the headline, and
`reasons` and `advice` say why and what to do: the page lists them in
the nav log (app.planning.no_altitude).
NavLogError.title: NavLogError

NearbyMetar.description:
A field's nearest report within 30 nm, for one with none of its
own: the station, how far and which way from the field (true), its
METAR, and `near` where it is within 10 statute miles, close enough to
say the field's weather by it, approximately (vfr.weather).
NearbyMetar.title: NearbyMetar

NearbyPlace.description: A place near a field from Overture Maps' places (vfr.nearby).
NearbyPlace.title: NearbyPlace

NearestAirport.description:
A field near a position: how far and which way (true), its town,
elevation and longest open runway, and a frequency listed for it
(None where OurAirports lists none).
NearestAirport.title: NearestAirport

NoteCheckpoint.description:
`source` says where the text came from: "saved" is a pilot's own
earlier edit, "generated" a fresh model call, "error" that call
failing for this checkpoint alone (`description` is None then).
NoteCheckpoint.title: NoteCheckpoint

NoteError.description:
A failure that applies to every checkpoint the same way (a bad
key, an exhausted rate limit), sent once.
NoteError.title: NoteError

OnRoute.description:
Where and when the flight meets a hazard (app.exposure): the legs
it is on (0-based, Briefing.leg_fixes' -- the nav log's where the
page sent them), from how far along to how far (nm from the
departure), when the airplane gets there and leaves (ISO 8601 UTC),
and the hazard's own times -- valid from and to, and when it was
issued (a pilot report's, when it was made; a METAR's, when it was
observed). `when` is whether the airplane is in it while it is
valid, give or take half an hour; None for one with no valid times
(a pilot report, a report or forecast for a field).
OnRoute.title: OnRoute

OpenSquawk.description:
A squawk not yet fixed, and how far its 14 CFR 91.213(d)
determination reaches, where one was made.
OpenSquawk.title: OpenSquawk

OralCitation.description:
A passage an answer rests on, quoted word for word (checked), with
its source's title and where to read it.
OralCitation.title: OralCitation

OralEditions.description:
The editions the sources are: the eCFR's issue date and the day the
AIM was read.
OralEditions.title: OralEditions

OralFocus.description: An ACS element the mock oral examines: its code and its words.
OralFocus.title: OralFocus

OralGrade.description:
The student's answer graded: satisfactory, partial or unsatisfactory,
in a few sentences, the key points it missed, and the citations.
OralGrade.title: OralGrade

OralQuestion.description:
One examiner's question (app.oral), its answer and key points, the
citations that survived the check, and the sources to grade from.
`unsupported` where none did.
OralQuestion.title: OralQuestion

OralQuestionRequest.description:
The student's flight in a few lines (the page's own summary of its
plan and briefing), the ACS elements to examine, and the questions
already asked.
OralQuestionRequest.title: OralQuestionRequest

OwnAirplane.description:
The pilot's own airplane being flown, its records from the gateway;
left out for a stock profile, which has none.
OwnAirplane.title: OwnAirplane

PastFlight.description: One past flight's reports, for its track log and its replay.
PastFlight.title: PastFlight

PastFlightField.description: A landing field a past flight took off from or landed at.
PastFlightField.title: PastFlightField

PastFlightPoint.description:
A report of a past flight: when (s since 1970), where, its height
(GNSS where sent, ft; None on the ground), ground speed (kt), track
(degrees true) and climb (ft/min).
PastFlightPoint.title: PastFlightPoint

PastFlightSummary.description:
One of an airplane's flights of the last days (vfr.traffic.history):
where it went from and to, where the receivers heard that, and when.
PastFlightSummary.title: PastFlightSummary

PastFlights.description:
An airplane's last flights found, ten at most, newest first, from
adsb.lol's traces (Open Database License 1.0).
PastFlights.title: PastFlights

PatternEntry.description:
The altitude PATTERN_NM from a field landed at, against its pattern
altitude, ft MSL.
PatternEntry.title: PatternEntry

PersonalMinimums.description:
The weather the pilot will not take off or land in, each off (None)
until set (lib/minimums): the lowest ceiling, feet above the field;
the least visibility, statute miles; the most crosswind on the best
runway and the most surface wind, gusts included, knots.
PersonalMinimums.title: PersonalMinimums

Pick.description:
A pilot's own mark on the chart. `rated` is derived from the
rating, so a rated point can never describe itself as unrated.
Pick.title: Pick

PilotCurrency.description:
The pilot's currency from their logbook, as the gateway's
/api/logbook/currency gives it (in snake case): the dates are the
last days each holds, "yyyy-mm-dd".
PilotCurrency.title: PilotCurrency

PilotNotesForgotten.description: How many of one pilot's own notes went, as their account did.
PilotNotesForgotten.title: PilotNotesForgotten

PipelineRun.description:
A run of the training DAG. `error`, for one that failed: the
exception its failed task ended on, from that task's own log.
PipelineRun.title: PipelineRun

PipelineStatus.description:
configured: this planner knows where Airflow is and how to sign
in; reachable: it answered just now. `training`: whether the ratings
are enough to retrain on, None where it could not be worked out.
PipelineStatus.title: PipelineStatus

Pirep.description:
A pilot report near the route (vfr.weather.pireps_along_route):
when, how high, in what, the turbulence and icing it reports (the
intensity, as reported: "LGT", "MOD", "NEG"), and its own words.
Pirep.title: Pirep

PlaceFound.description:
A place a pilot typed for Nearest to find the fields near: an
airport, a town, a street address (vfr.geocode), and where it is.
PlaceFound.title: PlaceFound

PlateOverlay.description:
An approach's plate's plan view placed on the map (vfr.plates): the
FAA's plate of `name` in d-TPP cycle `cycle`, its picture at
/api/approach-plate/{cycle}/{ident}/{procedure}.png, black on clear,
north up between these latitudes and longitudes, as the plate's own
georeference places it; `fixes` the approach's fixes inside it;
`circling` whether the plate publishes circling minimums, so a pilot
flying the approach may circle to land on another runway.
PlateOverlay.title: PlateOverlay

PointOffFix.description:
A point named as the pilot's own point off the nearest fix a pilot
knows (vfr.fixes.frd_near): "VPBNG/095/14.2", its fix, its magnetic
course from it (a VOR's radial where `radial`), its distance, and its
name, "14.2 nm on 095° from VPBNG".
PointOffFix.title: PointOffFix

ProcedureDrawing.description:
One procedure drawn with the transition picked (vfr.procedures):
its lines, holds and fixes, from the CIFP of `cycle`.
ProcedureDrawing.title: ProcedureDrawing

ProcedureFix.description:
A fix of a drawn procedure: its `roles` on an approach (IAF, IF,
FAF, MAP, hold), the altitudes it is crossed at -- at or above
`min_ft`, at or below `max_ft`, at both where they are one -- and the
speed it is crossed at, `speed_limit` saying whether that is the
speed ("at"), a minimum ("min") or a maximum ("max"; ARINC 424-18
5.261). `missed` where it is on the missed
approach alone.
ProcedureFix.title: ProcedureFix

ProcedureHold.description:
A holding pattern of a drawn procedure, or its procedure turn: at `fix`, its inbound
course `inbound_deg` true, its turns right or left (`turn`), drawn to
a light airplane's size (vfr.procedures.HOLD_SPEED_KT).
ProcedureHold.title: ProcedureHold

ProcedureLine.description:
A line of a drawn procedure, its points latitude and longitude:
an approach's `transition`, its `final` and its `missed` approach; an
arrival's or departure's enroute `transition`, `common` route, or a
`runway` transition, `name` the transition's ("RW08").
ProcedureLine.title: ProcedureLine

ProcedureList.description:
A field's instrument procedures, approaches first, from the CIFP
of the AIRAC cycle that took effect on `cycle` (YYMMDD); none for a
field with none.
ProcedureList.title: ProcedureList

ProcedureSummary.description:
One of a field's instrument procedures in the FAA's CIFP
(vfr.procedures): `id` its coded identifier ("I08-Y"), `name` its
chart's title ("ILS Y RWY 08"), `runway` an approach's, and the
transitions a pilot picks from -- an approach's, an arrival's or a
departure's enroute ones -- and an arrival's or departure's runway
transitions, which are drawn with it.
ProcedureSummary.title: ProcedureSummary

ProfileAirspace.description:
A Class B, C or D the route passes through: where along it, from
its floor to its ceiling (feet MSL; the ceiling None where the FAA's
file has none).
ProfileAirspace.title: ProfileAirspace

PyramidPass.description:
A pass of `python -m vfr.charts pyramid` under way: sheets done of
the sheets it set out to render, and the one it is on.
PyramidPass.title: PyramidPass

PyramidProgress.description:
One kind of chart's tile pyramid for a cycle. What finished passes
have left -- the sheets rendered, when the last finished, the tiles
written -- and the pass under way, if any. `complete` is every sheet
the FAA publishes of the kind rendered; `missing` names the rest.
PyramidProgress.title: PyramidProgress

RecentError.description:
A failure the planner answered lately (app.errors): when (UNIX
seconds), the call, its status and its words.
RecentError.title: RecentError

RiskAssessment.description:
The risk assessment: its points, its level and its line ("Raised ·
8 points"), what to do at that level, and every factor counted.
RiskAssessment.title: RiskAssessment

RiskCheck.description: One of the checks only the pilot can answer, in its group.
RiskCheck.title: RiskCheck

RiskFactor.description:
What raises the risk (lib/frat): why it counts, its points, and
whether it makes the flight unlawful as planned (`stop`).
RiskFactor.title: RiskFactor

RouteAlong.description:
What a way meets along it: its weather strip, its mean wind (kt,
a tailwind positive) and its floor (ft, the highest ground with
14 CFR 91.119's 1,000 ft).
RouteAlong.title: RouteAlong

RouteBand.description:
A run of the weather a way meets (vfr.route_options._along): VFR,
marginal (MVFR), IFR or a thunderstorm, and how many minutes of the
flight it lasts, in the order flown.
RouteBand.title: RouteBand

RouteChip.description:
One choice on FPL's route line (the owner's redesign, 2026-10-26:
the route folding as a runway line does, a chip a way): its `key`
("none" the route as typed, "fuel" it with its fuel stops, else the
way's kind), the words on it -- the way's name and the stops it adds
-- the stops and fuel stops it puts in the address, and the hazards
it crosses by their index in RouteOptions.hazards.
RouteChip.title: RouteChip

RouteHazard.description:
What a way keeps clear of (vfr.route_options): its kind -- storm,
weather, marginal, sigmet, tfr, prohibited, terrain -- and its words.
RouteHazard.title: RouteHazard

RouteOption.description:
One way to fly the route (vfr.route_options): the points between
its ends in order, as the address's `stops` takes them -- turns as the
pilot's own points off a fix, fuel stops as fields (`fuel`) -- and the
kinds of way it is the best of, with its estimate of the flight. The
hazards it still crosses and the marginal weather it passes, by their
index in RouteOptions.hazards.
RouteOption.title: RouteOption

RouteOptions.description:
The ways to fly a route, the fastest first; what the straight line
crosses (`direct`), what is at its ends (`ends`) and what the pilot's
own route crosses and passes (`current`, `current_marginal`), by index
in `hazards`; and the sources that could not be read now (`unchecked`).
RouteOptions.title: RouteOptions

RouteProfile.description:
The route's side view (vfr.profile): its length, the ground under
it, and the controlled airspace it passes through.
RouteProfile.title: RouteProfile

RouteStopField.description:
A field along the route to stop at, for the map's Stops (vfr.fuelstops.along):
which flight it is on, how far along it and off the line, its fuel,
and the nearest food, bed and car to hire from Overture (vfr.nearby),
once read (`nearby_known`).
RouteStopField.title: RouteStopField

RouteStops.description:
The fields along a route to stop at, in route order, and how many
of them still have their places to be read (`pending`): asked again
until none.
RouteStops.title: RouteStops

RouteTfr.description:
A TFR within a few miles of the route and in force at some time
during the flight: how far along the route it is, whether the route
goes through it, and whether it is in force now.
RouteTfr.title: RouteTfr

RunwayEnd.description:
One end of a runway (vfr.pattern): its true heading, None for a
helipad, which way its traffic pattern is flown -- left unless the FAA
flags it right (14 CFR 91.126(b)(1)) -- and where it is.
RunwayEnd.title: RunwayEnd

RunwayPicks.description:
The runway ends the pilot picked, by field: `pattern` the
departure's runway out and every other field's runway in, `takeoff` a
stop's runway out ("24", as painted).
RunwayPicks.title: RunwayPicks

RunwayTurf.description:
A length of a runway of two surfaces that is turf, where the FAA's
remarks say which (vfr.remarks.runway_turf): from `from_ft` to `to_ft`
feet along it from its `end`, `to_ft` None for the rest of it.
RunwayTurf.title: RunwayTurf

RunwayWind.description:
The reported wind on the end of a runway it favours, the one with
the most headwind (vfr.runway_wind): the headwind negative for a
tailwind, the crosswind positive from the right, and the crosswind
in the gusts where the report has them.
RunwayWind.title: RunwayWind

Services.description:
None for an agent this planner was not told the address of. The
webapp and its database are probed from here too -- its liveness
and its readiness group, which includes the database -- rather
than by the browser: a phone's probes queued behind its chart
tiles on one HTTP/1.1 connection pool and timed out, and the
console read "no answer" for a gateway that had just served it.
Services.title: Services

ShortField.description:
A POH's short-field takeoff or landing distances: a table per
weight, and how much a dry grass runway adds to the ground roll.
ShortField.title: ShortField

SpecialUse.description: One special-use area, as the FAA publishes it.
SpecialUse.title: SpecialUse

SpecialUseArea.description: One special-use area the route crosses.
SpecialUseArea.title: SpecialUseArea

StopField.description:
A field for the map's Stops, near the pilot or along a route: what
it has of the four kinds -- the fuel it sells and its airframe and
engine repair from its Chart Supplement entry (NASR's APT_BASE), its
places to eat on the field and its flight schools from Overture
(vfr.nearby) -- and its phone (NASR's APT_CON).
StopField.title: StopField

StopFields.description:
The map's Stops: the fields with fuel, food, repair or a flight
school, nearest first round the pilot or in route order along it, and
how many fields still have their places to be read (`pending`): asked
again until none.
StopFields.title: StopFields

TerminalChart.description:
One of a field's charts in the d-TPP (vfr.publications): `kind` the
FAA's chart code -- APD the airport diagram, HOT its hot spots, LAH
land and hold short, IAP an approach, DP and ODP a departure, STR an
arrival, MIN the takeoff or alternate minimums -- `name` its title as
the FAA prints it, `url` its PDF.
TerminalChart.title: TerminalChart

Tfr.description: A TFR with its areas, for the map: a GeoJSON MultiPolygon.
Tfr.title: Tfr

TfrHere.description: A TFR over the point, and whether it is in force now.
TfrHere.title: TfrHere

TopOfClimb.description:
Where a climb tops out (TOC), and the climb's true airspeed and
ground speed on the way up to it (vfr.navlog.with_climbs).
TopOfClimb.title: TopOfClimb

TopOfDescent.description:
Where a descent starts (TOD): down from `altitude_ft` to `to_ft` --
the pattern altitude of the field landed at, the altitude an
approach's first fix is crossed at, or the next leg's lower level --
at `fpm`, three to one at the leg's ground speed, or steeper where
the climb before it left less room (vfr.navlog.with_descents).
TopOfDescent.title: TopOfDescent

Totals.description:
The trip's sums, and the fuel check: the legs' fuel plus the VFR
reserve (30 minutes by day, 45 at night -- `night` is None when no
departure time said which) against the aeroplane's usable fuel,
when it has one. `fuel_margin_gal` below zero is a flight the tanks
do not hold.
Totals.title: Totals

Traffic.description:
The airplanes ADS-B receivers hear near a point, from adsb.lol's
open data, under the Open Database License 1.0, which asks that the
map say so where it draws them.
Traffic.title: Traffic

TrafficAircraft.description:
One airplane in the air near the point (vfr.traffic): who, where,
how high -- the GNSS height where it sends one, else its pressure
altitude set on the nearest METAR's altimeter (vfr.traffic.on_altimeter),
or as sent where none is near (`pressure_altitude`) -- its track, speed
and climb, and how many seconds old its position is.
TrafficAircraft.title: TrafficAircraft

TrafficFound.description:
The airplanes in the air a pilot named by callsign, registration
or ICAO address (vfr.traffic.find); and, where none is in the air or
heard now, the FAA's record of the one named (vfr.traffic.registered),
to open its card all the same.
TrafficFound.title: TrafficFound

TrafficPattern.description:
How high a field's traffic pattern is flown (vfr.pattern):
`agl_ft` above the field, the FAA's own where `published`, else AC
90-66C's 1,000 ft for a propeller aeroplane; `altitude_ft` above sea
level where the field's elevation is known.
TrafficPattern.title: TrafficPattern

TrailPoint.description:
Where an airplane was: Unix seconds, its position, its height (None
on the ground).
TrailPoint.title: TrailPoint

TrainingReadiness.description:
Whether a retrain has enough to train the chart model on, asked
before one is started (app.chart_model.readiness): the ratings on a
detection the trainer would get (`usable`) against what it needs, how
many of the `rated` are on a point the chart reader no longer finds
(`off_detection`), and the routes whose chart is still being read,
which cannot be counted yet. `message` says it in a sentence.
TrainingReadiness.title: TrainingReadiness

VerdictItem.description:
One tab's finding: what it is, what was found in a line, and where
it is shown in full (a tab of the Brief and a section by its title).
VerdictItem.title: VerdictItem

VfrMinimums.description:
14 CFR 91.155(a)'s basic VFR weather minimums: the flight
visibility, and the distance from clouds -- clear of them, or so far
below, above and to the side (5,280 ft is a statute mile).
VfrMinimums.title: VfrMinimums

VorCheck.description:
The airplane's last VOR check (14 CFR 91.171): its last good day and
whether its error was within limits.
VorCheck.title: VorCheck

VorPin.description: A VOR, VOR/DME or VORTAC in the map's view (NASR's NAV_BASE).
VorPin.title: VorPin

WaypointPin.description:
A VFR waypoint on the sectional (VPBNG), for the map's diamond: a
tap names it, and with a route open puts it in the stops.
WaypointPin.title: WaypointPin

WindsPeriod.description:
A winds and temperatures aloft forecast's period (AC 00-45H, the
Winds and Temperatures Aloft Forecast (FB)):
valid at `valid_at`, for use from `use_from` to `use_to`, ISO UTC.
WindsPeriod.title: WindsPeriod

get.description:
This service has no pages. The front end is built into the Spring
Boot gateway's jar and served from there, which is also the only
thing that calls this -- so this answers a health probe and says
where the UI went.

The stock performance profiles (data/aircraft/*.json) the nav log
can be computed for -- a pilot's own aeroplane overrides the cruise
TAS and fuel burn on top of one of these, see /api/navlog. Kept for
an hour at most (SHARED_CACHE): this is the picker's list; the nav
log's figures come from the profile on the server.

The field's aerial photo from the USGS National Map's imagery
(public domain), framed on its runways (vfr.airport_photos.aerial):
asked of the USGS once and kept, a week in the browser.

503.description: The USGS imagery could not be had

get.description:
The airport diagram cropped to its runways, for the card's
thumbnail: where the field's runway ends are (vfr.pattern's, NASR's
surveyed thresholds) placed on the diagram by its own latitude and
longitude labels, else its runway-thick strokes (vfr.publications).
404 where it has none, or its runways cannot be found on it -- the
card draws its own sketch then.

404.description: No diagram, or its runways not found on it

get.description:
The FAA's airport diagram for the field, from the d-TPP cycle in
force (`airport_diagram_cycle` on its card), as a picture for the card
to show and a finger to pinch in on: its PDF drawn once and kept for
the cycle (vfr.publications). 404 for a field with none -- most small
ones -- for any cycle but the one in force, and while the FAA cannot
be reached.

404.description: No diagram for the field in that cycle

get.description:
The field's photo from the ground (`airport_photos_of`), fetched from
Wikimedia Commons once and kept, a week in the browser.

404.description: No such field, or no free photo of it

get.description:
One US airport's card, by any ident it goes by (C81, KC81, KDLH).

`airspace_class` is the class of the airspace at the surface at the
field: B, C or D, E in a Class E surface area, G where the ground is
uncontrolled (vfr.airspace.surface_class_at).
`towered` is whether it lists a tower frequency. A field with no
reporting station has no `metar`; `weather_unavailable` is set only
when the weather service could not be asked.

The wind forecast at a field for a time -- a flight's arrival, for
the runway it will find in use then, at the owner's pick (2026-10-20):
its own TAF's prevailing wind, else the nearest TAF's within 30 nm.
Null where none covers that time; a 503 where the forecasts cannot be
had.

parameters.description: When, ISO 8601; a naive time is UTC.
parameters.name: at

schema.description: When, ISO 8601; a naive time is UTC.
schema.title: At
Response Airport Forecast Wind Api Airport  Ident  Forecast Wind Get

get.description:
The pictures an airport's card swipes through behind its diagram, at
the owner's ask ("airport photos swipe behind the airport diagram
thumbnail", 2026-10-23): its aerial (/api/airport-aerial, every US
field's, from the USGS) and its Wikipedia article's photo where there
is a free one (vfr.airport_photos).

The field's instrument procedures -- its approaches, arrivals and
departures, with the transitions of each -- from the FAA's CIFP for
the AIRAC cycle in force (vfr.procedures), for the route's Procedures
to offer. None for a field the CIFP has none for, as most small ones.

503.description: The FAA's procedure file could not be had

get.description:
One of the field's procedures drawn for the map, with the
transition picked (`transition`, one of its `transitions`; none for an
approach from vectors): its lines, holds and fixes, each fix with the
altitudes and speed it is crossed at (vfr.procedures.procedure_drawing).

404.description: No such procedure at the field

503.description: The FAA's procedure file could not be had

get.description:
An approach's plate's plan view placed on the map for the approach
picked (vfr.plates): where its picture goes, made once a cycle from the
FAA's d-TPP plate and its own georeference, and whether it publishes
circling minimums. 404 where the field has no plate for it, the plate
has no georeference, or the FAA cannot be reached.

404.description: No plate for the approach, or its plate's fixes do not place it

503.description: The FAA's procedure file could not be had

get.description:
What a field offers a pilot who lands there, for a stop's card: its
fuel, fees, parking, repair and oxygen and its courtesy car from the
FAA's airport file and remarks (vfr.faa_data.airport_services,
vfr.remarks.service_notes), and the places to eat, sleep and hire a
car near it (vfr.nearby). Its own request, not the card's: Overture's
first read of a field is a second or two, which the card's weather
and runways do not wait on.

The landing fields inside the map's view, the ones that report
first and then the biggest -- at most `limit` of them, since a whole
state holds thousands and the map only lays a tap target over each --
with each one's flight category from its METAR, for a weather chip on
the ones that report: the limit drops small fields with nothing to
show, never a chip a pilot saw a zoom further out -- and each one's
class of airspace at its surface, for its mark.
The METARs are the national cache already in memory; with the
weather service out the fields come back without, as fields with no
station do. With `reporting`, only the fields that report, before
the limit: what the map asks once for a whole route's box, so its
chips are there before the pilot zooms in on any of it.

Every US airport the search answers with, for the app to search on
the phone itself as a pilot types (vfr.airports.search_index): its
answers there at once, where each letter's question waited on this
planner, a second and more while it planned a route. Gzipped as it is
kept -- about 530 KB, from 1.8 MB -- and the same for every pilot until
OurAirports' table changes, so kept a day by the browser and the CDN
(PlannerProxyController passes both headers on). `v`, the shape the app
reads, unused here: in the address, so a day's copy of an older shape
is not taken for this one.

The landing fields nearest a position -- own ship's, for the map's
Nearest -- the nearest first: how far and which way, each one's
longest open runway, a frequency listed for it, its flight category
where it reports, and its class of airspace at the surface, as the
map's marks have it.

DEP/DEST's own autocomplete -- every airport whose ident or name
starts with `q`, for the route inputs to suggest as a pilot types.
Runs against the same in-memory OurAirports table the real lookup
uses, not a second data source that could drift from it. With
`fixes`, a stop's: the named fixes and navaids whose ident starts with
it too, after the airports -- VFR waypoints first (vfr.fixes). `near`,
the route's points as "lat,lon;lat,lon": of an ident's navaids in two
places, the one the route would fly over (fixes.find_navaid), as the
stop typed will be -- the row named the other where they differed.
Kept for an hour at most (SHARED_CACHE): these are suggestions, and
the stop picked is looked up afresh when the route is planned.

What is ahead of own ship in the air (vfr.alerts): the Class B, C
and D, special-use areas and TFRs its track goes into in the next five
minutes, and the ground or an obstacle it comes within 500 ft of in
the next minute. Nothing under 40 kt, on the ground. Advisory, from
the phone's GPS: not a TAWS.

parameters.description: True track over the ground, degrees
parameters.name: track

schema.description: True track over the ground, degrees
schema.title: Track

get.description:
The airspace over a point, from the ground to FL600, in bands
(vfr.airspace_at): each class's floor and ceiling in feet MSL, its
VFR weather minimums by day and by night (91.155), what it takes to
enter and what the aeroplane must carry -- with the Class B Mode C
veil the point is in, and the special-use areas and TFRs over it;
and the point named off the nearest fix (vfr.fixes.frd_near), for the
route. The ground, the shapefile and the two feeds are read at once.

The Class B, C and D inside the map's view (vfr.airspace_map), for
the map to draw over the chart: each volume's lines from the FAA's own
shapefile, so they lie on the chart's printed ones, with its floor and
top for the label the chart prints. None where the FAA's airspace
cannot be had: the chart's own lines are still under the map.

The IFR alternate for a flight arriving at `dest` at `eta` (UTC when
naive): whether the destination needs one (14 CFR 91.169(b), the
"1-2-3" rule, from its TAF an hour either side of the ETA), the
pilot's `alternate` checked against its minimums at the ETA there
(91.169(c)), and the nearest fields with a TAF that will do, each
reached at `tas_kt` from the destination (vfr.alternates).

The plan view of an approach's plate placed on the map
(`airport_procedure_plate`), as a picture: black on clear, north up,
for the cycle in force.

404.description: No plate placed for it in that cycle

get.description:
Everything the nav log's own leg math doesn't cover: adverse
conditions (SIGMET/AIRMET), current conditions (METAR) and
forecast (TAF-derived ceiling/visibility) along the route, and
each airport's runways and radio frequencies, its traffic pattern
(vfr.pattern) and the class of the airspace over it, for its
pattern card and the radio calls.

The forecast is for the flight: from `depart` (now when not given;
UTC when naive) to an hour past arrival, `ete_min` after it (two
hours when not given). It used to be read at the moment of asking,
whatever time the pilot was planning to go. With stops (`stops`,
"KDSM,KLNK"), along every hop and for every airport landed at.

Each hazard says where and when the flight meets it (`on_route`,
app.exposure): on the nav log's legs where the page sends them --
`fixes`, its points "lat,lon;lat,lon", `leg_min` each leg's ETE and
`ground_min` each leg's minutes on the ground after it -- else on
the route's own legs, the flight's time shared out by distance.

The chart the map draws, for a map with no route on it yet: the
planner's page opens on a search bar over the chart, as Maps does.
The map asks for no tile before this answers, so it may be kept
(CHART_CACHE) and served from the CDN's edge.

Any kind of chart by its key (`chart_layers` on the course lists
them): `sec`, `tac`, `ifr_low`, `ifr_high`, `ifr_area`. What the
map's layers draw from.

The FAA's own GeoTIFF of each sheet, rendered into a {z}/{x}/{y} tile
pyramid (vfr.charts -- downloaded once per 56-day chart cycle) and
cached on disk; the same tiles the detector reads. A tile pyramid is
what makes each chart a plain Leaflet tile layer: edge-only fetches
on a pan, the previous zoom's tiles scaled under the zoom animation,
a prefetch ring. 204 where no sheet covers the tile, which the layer
leaves blank. The sectional and the TAC had routes of their own
under older names, which nothing called any more.

post.description:
Fetch and render the FAA's current chart cycle now, in a
subprocess of the planner's own -- the same job it runs daily by
itself. `started` is False when one is already running.

A pilot's own edit to a checkpoint's identification note: what
they see at that place from now on. Other pilots keep the shared
note; where nobody can sign in, this becomes the shared note.

One "how to spot it" line per checkpoint, as newline-delimited
JSON (each line one app.schemas.CheckpointNoteMessage), so a slow
LLM call on checkpoint 3 does not hold up checkpoints 1 and 2 that
already arrived.

Two different kinds of failure, reported two different ways. A
single checkpoint's own LLM call failing for a reason specific to
it does not take the rest of the stream down -- every other
checkpoint is independent and still worth generating, so that one
gets its own per-checkpoint "error" line and the loop moves on.
GLOBAL_ANTHROPIC_ERRORS is the opposite case: a bad key or an
exhausted rate limit fails identically for every checkpoint, so
it's reported once as a single stream-level "error" (for one
banner instead of the same text repeated per row) -- but the
stream itself keeps going: every remaining checkpoint still gets
its own per-checkpoint "error" line too, just without spending a
call to learn what's already known. A pilot still gets a row to
type a note into for every checkpoint, not just the ones that
happened to come before the failure.

A POST, not a GET: every checkpoint without a note is a billed
Claude call and a write, which a GET invited from anything that
prefetches a link, and which the gateway's rules left public in
every deployment. The caller's own edit is what they see where they
made one; generation only ever fills the shared note.

delete.description:
A pilot's own notes, every one, taken out as their account is
deleted (the webapp's DELETE /api/me). Asked by the webapp alone:
its proxy does not forward this path, and the pilot is named by the
header it sets from the session. The shared notes stay.

get.description:
Scored candidates and the subset worth flying, hop by hop along
the whole route: fast once each hop's chart has been read, a few
seconds for its first time.

get.description:
Every Class B airport: where it is, and what the weather is doing
there now and what it is forecast to do.

`flight_category` is the METAR's own (VFR, MVFR, IFR, LIFR), not
this project's arithmetic -- it is what the reporting station
published, and a pilot already reads it that way. None where the
field has no current report.

What the chart draws at a point, so a hand-marked checkpoint is
categorised from the pixels rather than from whatever the dropdown
happened to be left on.

Just the course line and its endpoints, through any stops.

Separate from detection so the chart can draw a line the instant two
idents are entered. Reading tiles takes seconds even on the fast
path, and there is no reason a pilot should watch an empty map for
them.

And the route's slow parts are started here, the first thing the web
app asks for a route: the chart's read and the ground under it, on
threads of their own (app.prefetch), so the nav log asked for beside
this finds them under way or done.

post.description:
A saved flight debriefed against its flown track (web/src/lib/debrief,
ACS PA.VI.A): leg by leg the altitude and the course held, each
checkpoint's time against its estimate, and the altitude entering
each field's pattern -- each with its mark against the tolerance --
the profile, the line for the map and notes on what does not fit.
`debrief` is null where the track never flew faster than taxiing.
The fields' pattern altitudes are the planner's own (the card's).

get.description:
Detections as newline-delimited JSON, one line per block; each
line is one app.schemas.DetectMessage.

Blocks advance along the course, so the map fills from the departure
end and a pilot can start judging the first thirty miles while the
rest of the corridor is still being read. Airports come first, in
their own line, because they are a local file lookup and cost
nothing to produce.

The landmarks come from the shared per-route job (app.detection);
only the pick-matching is per-request, because picks change between
requests and the chart does not.

Each carries the chart model's score (app.chart_model) where the
corridor has been read whole already, which is every time but a
route's first: a detection's features count its neighbours, and a
block still being read does not have them all yet.

Which of the services the console links to are running.

`available` is false where there is no sidecar to ask, which is how
the console knows to stop offering to start anything rather than
offering a button that will fail.

post.description:
Start one of the four, if it is not already up.

Already running is a success, not an error: the console calls this
on every click so a link always works, and the common case is that
there was nothing to do.

get.description:
The diversion drill (web/src/lib/diversion, ACS PA.VI.C): from a point
to a field, in the planner's air on the way there at `altitude_ft` --
the winds and temperature aloft for the hour (vfr.weather, the FD
period for `depart`, now by default), the airplane's true airspeed and
burn in that air (vfr.performance) and the variation (vfr.magnetic,
the WMM) -- the true course and distance, the wind triangle, the
magnetic heading, ground speed, time and fuel, each step in words;
and the student's estimates (`mh`, `gs`, `ete`, `fuel`) checked
against it, each within the drill's allowance or not.

The pages of one of the FAA's charts in force -- by its address on
aeronav.faa.gov, as a card lists it (`procedures`, the Chart
Supplement's) -- for the app to show them itself rather than leave for
the FAA's site: every page of an approach or a departure, of one of
the FAA's booklets (a region's takeoff minimums) the pages naming
`airport`, of a Chart Supplement entry each of its pages. 404 for any
other address; 502 while the FAA cannot be reached, which the edge
does not keep as it keeps a 404.

One page of one of the FAA's charts in force as a picture, drawn
once and kept for its edition, as the airport diagram's is.

502.description: The FAA could not be reached

get.description:
A restaurant's stars, reviews and photos from Google Places, by its
name where Overture places it; a 404 where the deployment has no key,
or Google finds no place there, and the card shows the row as it is.

The route's checkpoints as a ForeFlight content pack (app.foreflight),
for ForeFlight's own link to the pack, or to download. `route` is its
idents dash-joined, KORD-KDLH or C81-KRYV-KDLH, and the checkpoints
are the planner's own selection for it; `file`, the pack's name, which
ForeFlight takes from the end of the address. A 422 for a route it
cannot read.

ForeFlight's downloader asks for the file several times over and
wants its size: so the same address is always the same bytes, a Range
is answered with a 206 of just those bytes, and the size goes with
every answer (a 416 for a range past the end).

post.description:
The Go / No-Go for a route: each finding -- the weather, the TFRs and
special-use airspace, the altitude, the fuel, the runways, the weight
and balance and the risk -- with where it is said in full, and the
line over them; the risk assessment and the weight and balance it
counted, for the Brief's own pages. The rules are web/src/lib/verdict's
and the modules it is fed from, ported to app.gonogo; the pilot's
minimums, loading, ticks, currency and own airplane's records come in
the ask.

get.description:
A hold's entry (web/src/lib/holding, AIM 5-3-8): for an airplane
heading `heading` to the fix of a hold on the inbound course `inbound`
with `turns`, the entry by the AIM's sectors and its steps in words,
and the other entry where the heading is within 5 degrees of a
sector's edge; given a true airspeed, a wind (both the course's
reference, magnetic as a clearance gives it) and the altitude, the
inbound and outbound headings and the outbound time that make the
inbound leg a minute (a minute and a half above 14,000 ft MSL).

A flight that leaves and lands at the same airport -- the pattern,
practice approaches, an hour's sightseeing: no course and no legs to
plan, so its totals are the time aloft at the aeroplane's cruise burn,
with the fuel check a route's has (the start and taxi allowance, the
VFR reserve by day or by night, the usable fuel). Night is judged at
the field at both ends of the time aloft, from now where no
departure time is given (planning.flight_totals). A 422 for a route
that is not one airport to itself.

post.description:
Two-way radio failure under IFR (web/src/lib/lostComms, 14 CFR
91.185): the routes in the rule's order, the altitude on each segment
-- the highest of assigned, the minimum for IFR operations and
expected, expected only from the segment it applies from -- and when
to leave the clearance limit. A POST for the segments' list; it
changes nothing.

get.description:
When the planner fetched what the map's weather layers are drawn
from, for the map's settings to say how old each is: the METARs
(aviationweather.gov's METAR file, held and refreshed by vfr.weather)
and the TFRs (tfr.faa.gov).

The deployment's Google Maps Platform key for the Map Tiles API,
for the browser's own session and tile requests (a browser key,
restricted to this site's address in Google Cloud); a 404 where there
is none, and the map offers no Google overlay.

Every algorithm anyone has actually trained for this problem,
not just the sklearn family retrain() grid-searches: the promoted
model's own comparison against Ridge/GradientBoosting/a dummy
"predict the mean" baseline, plus PyTorch/TensorFlow/Spark's own
candidates (vfr.model_candidates), when they exist.

Each entry names its own metric rather than pretending they are
all the same number: the sklearn family's own selection already
runs 5-fold CV (cv_mae), while the new candidates report a single
held-out split's MAE (held_out_mae) -- except Spark, whose own
CrossValidator gives it a real cv_mae too. Blending these into one
unlabeled column would overstate how comparable they actually are.

The VORs inside the map's view, and with `fixes` the fixes of the
low-altitude enroute chart there too (vfr.fixes), at most `limit` of
each: the hexagons and the triangles the map draws over the chart.
The map asks for the fixes only close in, where they do not scatter
over the whole chart.

Altitude and the dead-reckoning legs, as newline-delimited JSON --
the slow half, because it reads terrain, the obstacle file, the
airspace shapefile and live winds; asked for separately so none of
that delays the chart. Each line is one app.schemas.NavLogMessage.

Streamed rather than a single blocking response so a pilot sees the
table fill in as it goes rather than a blank screen: a "stage" line
before each real piece of work (scoring, the altitude plans), an
"altitude" line the moment those are decided -- the four plans and
the one chosen (altitude_choice, see /api/plan) with it -- one "leg"
line per leg, then one "done" line with the totals, which need
every leg in before they mean anything. Its own implementation, not
a wrapper over /api/plan: that one commits to a single synchronous
JSON response, and mixing a streaming and a non-streaming contract
into one function would compromise both. The overlap is the same
handful of calls into app.planning and vfr.navlog either way.

An unflyable route (some leg with no legal cruising altitude at all)
is reported as an "error" line, not an HTTP error status -- by the
time that's known, a 200 and a stream of NDJSON have already gone
out, and an HTTP status can't change after that.

post.description:
The student's answer graded against the question's answer and the
sources it was asked from (`source_ids`, as the question gave them).

One question on one of the `focus` ACS elements, set in the flight
`plan` describes, not one of those already `asked`; its answer from
the sources and the passages it quotes, each checked word for word.
A 503 where the sources cannot be had, a 502 where the examiner
cannot be reached.

get.description:
Where a place typed is, for Nearest to find the fields near it
rather than near own ship: the airports whose ident or name starts
with it, the towns that do (the Census gazetteer), and a street
address where it starts with a house number (the Census geocoder) --
each with where it is (vfr.geocode).

The whole plan: course line, every scored candidate, the selected
checkpoints, and a nav log leg between each consecutive pair.

altitude_ft is optional. Omitted, vfr.altitude works out each leg's
own legal altitudes -- clear of terrain and obstacles, under the
Class B shelf over that leg alone and the aircraft's service
ceiling, on the hemispheric rule for that leg's own course
-- and vfr.navlog makes four plans of them: the lowest, the
highest, the fastest for the winds aloft, and the one that burns the
least fuel, climb and cruise. altitude_choice picks
which one the legs fly -- the fastest unless asked otherwise, the
plan a pilot with the winds in hand picks (it was the lowest, as the
predictable one) -- and the reasoning comes back with it, since
"why am I at 6,500" is a question a pilot will actually ask.

aircraft names a stock profile; cruise_tas_kt, fuel_burn_gph,
usable_fuel_gal, climb_tas_kt, climb_fuel_burn_gph and
cruise_power_pct (the power the cruise figures are at), when given,
are a pilot's own aeroplane's numbers laid over it. Each leg flies
them in its own air: the cruise figures are the aeroplane's at a
reference altitude on a standard day, and the forecast temperature
at the leg's altitude gives the density altitude they are flown at
(vfr.performance). depart, an ISO time (UTC when naive), picks the
winds-aloft forecast period the legs are flown on -- the 6-, 12- or
24-hour product, whichever is valid closest to the departure;
without it, the 6-hour product, i.e. about now -- and whether the
fuel reserve is the day or the night one.

post.description:
Starts one run of the training DAG through Airflow's own API -- the
same thing the AWS retrain-trigger Lambda does: the chart model
(retrain, evaluate, promote) and the landmark model where it has the
ratings (collect, engineer features, retrain, evaluate, promote).
This service has no scikit-learn of its own on purpose (see
requirements.txt), so it cannot train in-process; without Airflow
reachable the answer says how to run the pipeline by hand.

Checked first (app.chart_model.readiness): with too few ratings to
learn from, it says so and what to do, a 409, rather than starting a
run that ends in Airflow minutes later with the same news in its
log. Then the chart model's table is written from the ratings as
they are now, which the run trains on.

get.description:
The ways to fly from `dep` to `dest` in the airplane, at the owner's
ask ("smart to reroute for fastest time along safe weather, over
terrain, best tailwinds, refueling", 2026-10-23): each its points in
order for the address's `stops`, its fuel stops, and its distance,
minutes and fuel, from a coarse read the plan then checks leg by leg.
It only suggests.

The route's side view: the ground under it every 2 nm and the
Class B, C and D airspace it passes through, floor and ceiling, along
the whole route through its stops (vfr.profile) -- for the page to
draw the plan's altitudes, climbs and descents over.

The fields along the route to stop at, for the map's Stops, at the
owner's ask ("a button to show food, fuel, rest options along the
route they can pick from", 2026-10-23): every public field near each
flight's line (vfr.fuelstops.along), each with its courtesy car (the
FAA's remarks) and the nearest food, bed and car to hire where its
places have been read (vfr.nearby.kept). Those not yet read are read
on the planner's pool and counted in `pending`; the page asks again
until none is. The times and the fuel at each are the page's, from
the plan's own figures per mile.

One snapshot of the whole stack, for Settings' Dev tab. The
network probes run side by side so a service that is down costs one
timeout, not one per service.

The public fields along a route with fuel, food, repair or a flight
school, in route order, for the map's Stops while a course is drawn:
those no more than STOP_OFF_COURSE_NM off each flight's line, each
with its miles from its flight's departure, those it adds and how far
off the course it is; what they have as round the pilot.

The public fields round a position with fuel, food, repair or a
flight school, nearest first, for the map's Stops (the owner's one
sheet for them near the pilot and along a route, 2026-10-27), within
`nm` (the sheet's 10, 25, 50 or 100). A field's places are Overture's
(vfr.nearby), read on the planner's pool where they have not been and
counted in `pending`; a field selling fuel or with a repair shop is
listed at once, its places to come (`places_known`), and the page
asks again until none is pending.

Every temporary flight restriction in force or to come, for the
map: each NOTAM's areas, when, how high and why (vfr.tfr). A 502 when
tfr.faa.gov does not answer, for the map to say so rather than draw
a sky with none.

The airplanes in the air within `radius` nm of a point (at most 165),
from adsb.lol (Open Database License 1.0), and how many seconds old
the answer is: for knowing what is about, not for avoiding it. A 503
where adsb.lol has not answered for a minute.

Where each airplane is based, for the Aircraft tab's "based at"
filter (vfr.traffic.based): the field its last flights begin and end at
most; the ones not known yet looked up in the background, pending.

The airplanes in the air a pilot names -- UAL2088, N174HA, a0b7d8 --
to track one; with none in the air or heard now, the FAA's record of a
US airplane named by its N-number or address, its card opened all the
same (`registered`). Where adsb.lol cannot be asked now, what can be
shown all the same, `checked` false: the FAA's record of the one named,
which needs no asking. It was a 503, which the pilot read as "Couldn't
search" for an airplane the registry knew (N654FL, 2026-10-11).

An airplane being tracked: what it is, the field it took off from
and its track today (vfr.traffic.flight); no track where its trace
cannot be had.

An airplane's last ten flights found, newest first, as FlightAware
lists them (vfr.traffic.history): from adsb.lol's recent trace and its
archive of past days', about six weeks, a fortnight at a time. With
`until` and `before`, the ones before those listed; with `until` alone,
those on and before a day picked. A day that cannot be had now is left
out and counted.

get.description:
One of those flights' reports, for its track log and its replay
(vfr.traffic.past_flight); 404 where it is not one of them.

An airplane's state now, for the alerts a pilot sets on it -- takes
off, lands, comes near (vfr.traffic.status): from adsb.lol's recent
trace, seconds old, which costs none of its API's turns. A 503 where
that trace cannot be read now.

The route a flight number is scheduled to fly -- TJSJ to KORD for
UAL2088 -- and whether the airplane at lat/lon is on or near it, from
Virtual Radar Server's route database (CC0); null for a callsign that
is not an airline's flight number or one it does not know. Not the
flight plan filed for today's flight.

get.description:
The VFR waypoints inside the map's view (vfr.fixes), at most
`limit`: the magenta flags the sectional prints round busy airspace,
for the map to mark each with a diamond a pilot can tap and route
through. GPS waypoints and the rest of NASR's fixes are left out:
they are not on a VFR chart.
